decoded:
Tier A
Tier B

Catering quote from Saffron Bites just came in. For main spread on the 15th they are offering two tiers.

Tier A: $48 per head includes seared tuna canapés, braised short rib station, full dessert display.

Tier B: $37 per head swaps short rib for mushroom Wellington station, cuts dessert display to just chocolate torte, berry pavlovas.

My read: we need to stick with Tier A for primary sponsor dinner in Veridian Room but could potentially use Tier B for general attendee reception in Atrium if budget gets squeezed.

However, their minimum for any single service is 70 guests.

If Veridian Room headcount is under 70, we need to pad with organizing committee members to hit minimum.

^ Only move people from Atrium list if absolutely necessary; we promised them full experience.

For Atrium, if count is between 70 and 90, Tier B is approved.

If count exceeds 90, switch back to Tier A for them as well, as the per-head cost difference shrinks with volume and the upgrade is worth it for the larger crowd.

On timing, they need final menu selection and guaranteed guest numbers by 5 p.m. this Thursday, the 7th.

They offered 3% discount if we wire 50% deposit by Friday at noon instead of the following Monday.

Remaining balance due on the 13th.

^ Confirm wire details with Aris in Finance; use vendor code CAT-882.

^ If discount applies, note it explicitly on payment authorization.

^ Double-check their proposal includes late-night snack delivery for tech crew at 11 p.m.

That is a separate order for 15 boxed meals, not part of per-head calculation.

^ If we go with Tier B anywhere, get written confirmation from Saffron Bites that all nut-based ingredients are excluded from mushroom Wellington filling.

Last year incident with pine nut puree cannot be repeated.

Their standard recipe includes it, so this requires specific amendment.
